ksbs.description: The automotive industry and the role of the autocare technician. Limits of autonomy and reporting channels.
Vehicle safety inspections and routine maintenance: manufacturers specifications or approved schedules. The use of vehicle specific data and the legal requirements for wear and serviceability.

Awareness of health and safety regulations, standards, and guidance and impact on role. Safe working procedures, COSHH, fire safety, good housekeeping, hazards and risks, manual handling, PPE, safety equipment and signage, slips, trips and falls, LOLER and PUWER.
Environment and sustainability guidance relevant to the occupation and the autocare technician's responsibilities. Recycling, reuse and safe disposal of waste.
Tools and equipment used in the automotive industry: purpose and operation.
Maintenance and storage methods for tools and equipment, including calibration checks.
Workplace instructions: purpose and use for inspection, maintenance and replacement.
Vehicle service records, owner's manuals and warranties: purpose and use.
Tyres: legislation, replacement, repair and technical information including tyre labelling, TPMS, sidewall markings and homologated fitments.
Steering systems: purpose, function and location of systems and components for inspection, removal and replacement.
Suspension systems: purpose, function and location of systems and components for inspection, removal and replacement.
Braking systems: purpose, function and location of systems and components for inspection, removal and replacement, including wheel bearings.
Emission control systems: purpose, function and location of systems and components for inspection, removal and replacement.
Vehicle heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems: purpose, function and location for inspection, maintenance and replacement.
Low voltage batteries, starting and charging systems: purpose, function and location.
Maintenance and replacement of low voltage batteries, starting and charging systems.
Awareness of ADAS and the impact of repair work, including static and dynamic calibration methods and equipment.

plannedActivities.instruction:
For suspension replacement and alignment preparation, use manufacturer information for a vehicle or a clearly labelled case study:
1. Explain whether the work could affect ADAS and identify the required checks.
2. Explain any relevant static and dynamic calibration methods and equipment, or why specialist advice is needed.
3. Record your information source and referral decision. Do not assume every repair requires calibration or carry out work beyond your authorised role.

For electrical diagnostic testing, use manufacturer information for a vehicle or a clearly labelled case study:
1. Explain whether the work could affect ADAS and identify the required checks.
2. Explain any relevant static and dynamic calibration methods and equipment, or why specialist advice is needed.
3. Record your information source and referral decision. Do not assume every repair requires calibration or carry out work beyond your authorised role.

For steering component replacement and alignment checks, use manufacturer information for a vehicle or a clearly labelled case study:
1. Explain whether the work could affect ADAS and identify the required checks.
2. Explain any relevant static and dynamic calibration methods and equipment, or why specialist advice is needed.
3. Record your information source and referral decision. Do not assume every repair requires calibration or carry out work beyond your authorised role.

For tyre wear and geometry investigation, use manufacturer information for a vehicle or a clearly labelled case study:
1. Explain whether the work could affect ADAS and identify the required checks.
2. Explain any relevant static and dynamic calibration methods and equipment, or why specialist advice is needed.
3. Record your information source and referral decision. Do not assume every repair requires calibration or carry out work beyond your authorised role.

plannedActivities.instruction: During the ADAS activity, explain passive and active driver assistance and levels of autonomy. Give one example of each and explain the driver responsibility and referral limits. Record the explanation in the existing work/findings field; the tutor checks understanding.

Use a vehicle or clearly labelled case study from the suspension/alignment task. Identify one affected driver-assistance feature and explain whether it is passive or active. Explain the driver’s responsibilities and, within the levels of driving automation, identify the level supported by the information provided. Name the information source; do not assume features or capabilities that the example does not show.

Use a clearly labelled driver-assistance electrical fault case. Identify the feature, whether it is passive or active, and how the described fault changes the warning or assistance available. Explain the driver’s responsibilities and, within the levels of driving automation, identify the level supported by the information provided. Name the information source; do not assume features or capabilities that the example does not show.

Use a clearly labelled steering/ADAS case. Compare a warning-only feature with an active assistance feature, and explain the difference for the driver. Explain the driver’s responsibilities and, within the levels of driving automation, identify the level supported by the information provided. Name the information source; do not assume features or capabilities that the example does not show.

Use a vehicle or clearly labelled case study from the tyre/geometry task. Identify a related driver-assistance feature and explain whether it warns the driver or actively assists. Explain the driver’s responsibilities and, within the levels of driving automation, identify the level supported by the information provided. Name the information source; do not assume features or capabilities that the example does not show.

ksbs.description: Awareness of electrified vehicle technologies and principles of operation, including high voltage battery and onboard charger condition monitoring.
Awareness of hydrogen-powered vehicle technologies and principles of operation, including storage and fuel-cell condition monitoring.
Safe working procedures for electrified vehicles, including high voltage systems and safe isolation.
Principles of customer care: pre- and post-vehicle service, identifying needs and handling challenging conversations.
Business operation considerations: efficiency, customer satisfaction, competitiveness, operational risk and ethical issues.
Vehicle parts costings and procurement: customer, organisation and vehicle needs.
Materials, resources and stock storage used in the automotive industry. Stock and resource management processes.
Principles of customer sales and financial compliance, including FCA and PCI requirements.
Principles of sales processes.
Team-working principles.
Principles of equity, diversity and inclusion in the workplace and the impact on work.
Verbal communication techniques: giving and receiving information and matching style to audience.
Written communication techniques, electronic and paper, using autocare industry terminology.
Information and digital technology, including email, collaboration packages, databases, digital interfaces, management information systems, point of sale, GDPR and cyber security.
Comply with health and safety procedures in the workplace in line with regulations, standards and guidance.
Prepare the vehicle and working area before the work activity.
Maintain and restore the work area during and on completion of the activity.
Store and maintain tools and equipment, including calibration checks, and return them to storage.
Access vehicle technical data to inform inspections and make judgements on wear and serviceability.
Comply with environmental and sustainability procedures and segregate resources for reuse, recycling and disposal.
